The flight time from California to Victoria is nearly the same for both teams – roughly 16 hours – but their journeys to the start of the season couldn’t be more different.It’s been smooth sailing for the Rams, with their collection of playmakersgrowing by the day. It’s a very different story for the 49ers: facing Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, not to mention the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks, at least twice this season is the least of their problems. Their offseason has been more than lightly turbulent: it’s been batshit crazy.Who would fall in love with a fake NFL player? Plenty of sensible peopleRead moreThe history of NFL scandals is Mariana Trench deep, and every season a unique calamity pops up.Meet Daejon Love, 49ers wide receiver, wealthy investor and a Casanova on the prowl. At least that’s what the 26 women Love allegedly defrauded out of $1.3m are said to have believed. Love, who it turns out is decidedly not a San Francisco 49er, was arrested last month by the FBI andhas been chargedwith conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. It’s unclear what is more bonkers: Love’s apparent audacity or the fact that none of the women he is said to have defrauded appear to have googled their new “NFL player” boyfriend.The 49ers organization is free of blame in the Love fiasco. But some of the dirt around the story will still rub off on them. The team will no doubt still be treated to “Sign Love” banners and memes every time one of their wideouts drops a catch.At least the 49ers head coach, Kyle Shanahan, was wearing his seatbelt in a July car crash in which he suffered injuries including a serious concussion and a broken nose, hand and ribs.Shanahan admitted he was at fault: he says he took his eyes off the road when he was searching for his dropped phone. The weirdness stemmed from 49ers brass failing to disclose the injuries Shanahan had suffered and details of the crash for 11 days after it happened. Shanahan has been as clean as a whistle since he became 49ers head coach in 2017. The organization’s initial silence, knowing that Shanahan would need a slow return to training camp, made the situation appear more nefarious than it actually was.There was no way to hide 49ers owner Jed York’s mugshot a few weeks later though.York was arrestedafter he used a website to secure the services of a sex worker for $140 at an Ohio trailer park. That woman turned out to be an undercover cop. York, whose family is worth $8.5bn, was fined $1,150, spent a night in jail and now faces an investigation by the NFL under the league’s personal conduct policy. Of course, York is among the bosses of those running the investigation,so don’t expect himto get more than a slap on the wrist. As with the Love situation, the 49ers have landed unwelcome publicity, although this time the team’s owner is to blame. As if the 49ers wanted more attention over York’s arrest, Pro Football Hall of Famer and relationship expert Michael Irvin piped up in the owner’s defense.“Everybody’s paying for it. So, what are we doing? Why we gotta embarrass this man for $140?” Irvin said during aTwitch livestream. “People think: ‘You’re a billionaire. Why didn’t you go to high-end places?’ The high-end places get you in trouble all the time.”Until recently, the 49ers had evaded this level of bizarre in the Shanahan-John Lynch era. In the last few years, the 49ers have been a steady franchise whose chances of success usually end up stymied by a series of injuries to their best players.Sure, last year the team had to hire an expert todebunk the theorythat an electrical substation near the 49ers practice facility played a role in a buffet of injuries, including those to All-Pros Nick Bosa, Fred Warner, and George Kittle. So far this season, wideout Ricky Pearsall’s 2026 campaign is already over after he reaggravated a PCL injury, while rotational defensive lineman Sam Okuayinonu fractured his foot at practice in Melbourne. Those are big losses for San Francisco but most of their superstars are healthy for now.So, maybe, the script has flipped. The 49ers could be chaotic off the field but largely steady and healthy on it. If it means they win their first Super Bowl since the 1994 season, it’s a narrative their fans will take.Explore more on these topicsSan Francisco 49ersNFLUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: MLS’s transfer window and the spending line that keeps going up | MLS | The Guardian
description: Summer spending across the league’s 30 clubs has ballooned. Here are three takeaways from the league’s transfer window
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Summer spending across the league’s 30 clubs has ballooned. Here are three takeaways from the league’s transfer window
Content: Andrew Luiz joined Sporting Kansas City this summer for a fee that shattered the club’s previous record.Photograph: Reed Hoffmann/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAndrew Luiz joined Sporting Kansas City this summer for a fee that shattered the club’s previous record.Photograph: Reed Hoffmann/Getty ImagesMLSAnalysisMLS’s transfer window and the spending line that keeps going upCatalina BushSummer spending across the league’s 30 clubs has ballooned. Here are three takeaways from the league’s transfer windowTue 8 Sep 2026 13.00 EDTShareWith the shadow of the 2026 World Cup hanging over the league and a potential set of rule changes looming, Major League Soccer’s summer transfer window was one defined by uncertainty, diverse strategies and record spending. It was the fourth transfer window sinceMLSallowed clubs to purchase players from other clubs using traditional transfer fees rather than general allocation money (GAM), the intraleague currency system. The new rule, which is now being used more frequently, has helped account for rapid growth in league expenditure, as has increased GAM allotted to each club.These trends have been seen broadly over the last two seasons, but this past window took it to a new level, smashing the previous record for summer spending. This summer, MLS teams spent 65% more year-over-year, with a total of nearly $190m spent, accounting for 45% of the 2026 total. The above factors combined to create one of the most consequential transfer windows in MLS history, which may give a glimpse into the league’s future trajectory.Record spendingThis summer brought MLS to more than $410m spent on trades and transfers in 2026, which is more than double the 2023 total. Much of this growth came between 2024 and 2025, with the cash-for-player system accounting for $41m in transfers that were not previously possible. The introduction of this rule has not replaced GAM spending, but rather complemented it. MLS allows clubs to convert up to $3m in eligible transfer revenue to GAM per year, and the introduction of the cash-for-player rule has made hitting that $3m mark significantly easier. The end result: there’s much more GAM circulating the league now, enabling more teams to buy down cap hits, complete trades and do everything else a team can do with those funds.MLS spending on trades and transfersMLS has also seen growing income from outbound transfers. The league has now earned nearly $800m from player sales since 2022, with the departing players becoming younger and younger. This summer, six players aged 23 or younger left the league in deals worth $5m or more, with three of those players born in the United States.Lucas Herrington, a 19-year-old Australia international, left Colorado Rapids to join Hull City for a base fee of $17m.Zavier Gozo, meanwhile, joined Crystal Palace for $15m. Gozo, an American and a Real Salt Lake academy product, is the latest example of MLS’s academy pipeline producing top talent that is in high demand in some of the world’s largest leagues.Lionel Messi’s international retirement serves as a reminder: watch him while you still canRead moreSporting KC go full rebuildEarly last season, Sporting KC parted ways with Peter Vermes, the club’s head coach since 2009, and sporting director since three years before that. In September, the club hired David Lee, New York City FC’s sporting director, to the same position. They brought Raphaël Wicky in as head coach. And in January of this year, billionaire Peter Mallouk bought a controlling stake and became the club’s new majority owner. A new head coach, GM or owner can each have massive ramifications on how a club operates, but changing all three in the span of a year is a completely different challenge.When Lee joined, he inherited an operation that had long been run almost entirely by Vermes. It’s easy to paint the picture of Vermes as the old-guard veteran, skeptical of convoluted roster mechanisms and oblivious to analytics, while Lee represents the new-age GM, with City Football Group experience and a savvy understanding of MLS’s roster regulations. Though that may be an oversimplification, the facts are these: prior to Vermes’s dismissal, the club failed to spend a cent of GAM on trades between 2022 and 2025. In the three windows since then, they’ve spent $700,000 while also acquiring $6m through the sale of Dejan Joveljic via the cash-for-player mechanism. The club has also hired a new vice-president of data and analytics, Francisco Belo, from Nottingham Forest and is investing in their scouting operations. The new owner has helped things, too; Sporting KC, once one of the most frugal teams in MLS, have gone on a spending spree.Bar chart showing Sporting Kansas City spending levels over the last five seasons, with a big spike in 2026 spending.Under Lee’s tenure, the club’s cumulative spending on player acquisitions since 2022 has skyrocketed, from $18m to $56m. On average, Sporting KC spend about $2.9m in secondary transfer windows, which ranks 23rd in MLS. This summer, they spent a total of $27.2m. The investment was sorely needed, too, with the club rostering just 14 senior roster players at the beginning of the year. Additionally, with the sale of Joveljic and Lee’s decision to part ways with Spanish midfielder Manu García, the club spent part of the summer without a designated player (DP) or a U22-initiative player on the roster. These six coveted spots allow MLS teams to compete, and clearing every spot to make room for a complete rebuild is nearly unheard of.Lee did not fill all of them, despite that eye-popping expenditure. Instead, the club signed one DP in Andre Luiz for $18m and filled one of their U22 spots by signing Owen Wolff from Austin for $4.5m in cash. Despite in-progress data and scouting departments, the club still managed to add key pieces while retaining immense flexibility heading into next season.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWorld Cup wishlists, early movers, big clearouts: 2026 summer transfer window trendsRead moreUnfortunately, the current on-field product is paying the price for this extended rebuild. Sporting are last in MLS and flirting with one of the worst defensive records in league history. It’s not looking like it’s going to get better soon.Sprint season shake-upsWith MLS’s schedule change right around the corner, club decision-makers are already beginning to plan for the 2027 sprint season and beyond. Transitioning to a fall-to-spring schedule means the summer transfer window will only become more important, and with Larry Berg set to assume the role of commissioner, teams are preparing for change. While little is known about the proposed rule changes that could overhaul MLS roster construction, it’s clear some clubs are betting that relaxed restrictions are on the way – that would mean longer-term contracts and delayed pay structures in the short term. Conservative clubs, meanwhile, are taking care to not lock themselves into deals that could become an issue down the road.Chart showing the change in spending of all 30 MLS clubs, with Sporting KC and Colorado at the top with greater expenditures and Austin and Charlotte FC spending way less than previous windows.This divide in strategies can be seen in the aggressiveness of teams this summer. Sporting KC, St Louis City, and the Colorado Rapids all spent far above their usual budgets, with an average increase of $18.6m in expenditure.Others decided to play it safe. Los Angeles FC netted $14m this summer after spending just $525,000. Austin FC, another perennial high spender, are in the midst of their own rebuild and likewise decided to pursue flexibility over spending. Charlotte FC were the only side to spend nothing on transfer fees, but still managed to sign Allan Saint-Maximin while bringing in $6m from the sale of Kerwin Vargas.It remains to be seen which of these strategies proves most fruitful once the new season structure and rules go into place, but the disparity between approaches is stark. A near-equal amount of teams spent similar to their usual expenditures as those who spent above and those who spent below.It’s perhaps remarkable that despite this divide between MLS clubs, the league’s spending continues to grow so drastically. A year of change is surely ahead, but MLS has shown that increased investment is a given.Explore more on these topicsMLSSporting Kansas CityTransfer windowUS sportsanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham have been stalked. They’re far from alone in the WNBA | WNBA | The Guardian
description: Players generally welcome interacting with their fans. But as the league’s popularity surges, there are dangers to be aware of
Author: Stephanie Kaloi
Headline: Players generally welcome interacting with their fans. But as the league’s popularity surges, there are dangers to be aware of
Content: Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham have both had to deal with stalkers.Photograph: Christian Petersen/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCaitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham have both had to deal with stalkers.Photograph: Christian Petersen/Getty ImagesWNBACaitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham have been stalked. They’re far from alone in the WNBAPlayers generally welcome interacting with their fans. But as the league’s popularity surges, there are dangers to be aware ofStephanie KaloiTue 8 Sep 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 05.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCaitlin Clark spent most of the 2025 WNBA season sidelined with a series of injuries that forced her to miss more than 30 games. But she also spent part of the season (and the preceding offseason) quietly navigating a tumultuous and scary reality: a 55-year-old manwas stalking her, and he was convinced they were in a relationship.That man, Michael Lewis,was sentencedto two-and-a-half years in prison last July. Lewis sent Clark “hundreds” of messages – many of which were “threats and sexually explicit” – between 12 December 2024 and 11 January 2025. Lewis, who is from Texas, was arrested at a hotel in Indianapolis, where Clark plays for theIndiana Fever. The case took a toll on Clark: she said she feared for her safety and had changed her appearance in public.Cathy Engelbert’s WNBA tenure: the wins and losses that defined her seven yearsRead moreClark isn’t the only player in the WNBA who has had a stalker, and stalking isn’t limited to the pros. In 2024, a 40-year-old man pleaded guilty tostalking Paige Bueckers, who was then playing for the UConn Huskies; former Indiana Fever guard Syd Colson hasspoken about her own stalkerseveral times. As a college student at UCLA, Toronto Tempo’s Kiki Ricereceived “dozens” of messagesfrom a man who believed the pair shared something “magnetic.” In June, a 48-year-oldman was arrestedfor stalking Clark’s teammate Sophie Cunningham.The problem is not unique to the WNBA: NFL star Aaron Donaldwas stalkedby a woman who falsely claimed they were married. But the league’s rising popularity, the ever-present threat of misogyny and the fact that women are far more likely to be stalked than men mean the problem is one the league is unfortunately becoming more familiar with.That’s not to say that every fan interaction is negative; in fact, most are great for both parties. Earlier this month, the Portland Fire’s Emily Engstler told reporters that the team gets “recognized a decent amount.”Portland fans are “super respectful,” she added. That’s something Engstler “really appreciates,” and she likes the fan-athlete relationship to be a two-way street. “I think it’s not hard to be respectful to your fans and give them the time of day,” she added. “So I try to make sure I do it.”The fan-athlete relationshipisparasocial, Dr Shira Gabriel, professor of psychology at SUNY, University of Buffalo, says. But, she points out, parasocial relationships aren’t inherently bad, and we all have them.Gabriel, whose book Collective Effervescence will be released next year, studies these relationships. While writing her book, she found that researchers examining parasocial bonds “at first were looking for all the bad stuff and trying to find that these are the loneliest, most desperate people,” she says. “And if anything, the opposite is true.”Forming these bonds “is a part of being a healthy person in the modern world,” Gabriel says. “We have access to information about people that we would never have had when we were developing as a species.”She went on to point out that nearly all of us have some kind of parasocial bond, whether that’s keeping up with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, or attendingWNBAgames and following players on social media to find out more about their lives.Humans seek connection, Gabriel says. “If you’re a big WNBA fan, you can feel connected to the whole fandom, and that’s great,” Gabriel continues. “That’s an important thing for us. Again, we’re a really social species, and we want to have those connections … this is something that healthy people do and that increases the degree to which we can feel connected.”Those relationships begin to go wrong when “people sort of forget that the person who they have the bond with is an actual living and breathing human being, and you are sort of dehumanizing them” when you forget that, Gabriel says. “They’re just sort of this person online, and that opens up avenues for people to behave in ways or treat people in a way that they wouldn’t in their real life.”The risk factors that make someone more likely to escalate a parasocial relationship to stalking are similar to those that exist in real relationships, too.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I think the people who are doing this are people who are probably not particularly stable in other aspects of what they’re doing,” Gabriel says. “You’re not going to find somebody who is doing well in their lives, and is happy, and not suffering from severe mental illness, who mistakes these for real bonds and starts going after someone, just like you’re not going to date somebody who’s actually like a super healthy wonderful person and have them turn into a stalker who completely disrupts your life.“When that happens, that’s because this person is bringing some kind of real emotional baggage with them, and that’s what we would see with a parasocial bond, too.”A league source told the Guardian that the WNBA is well aware of all of these dynamics, and player safety is paramount. The league pays attention to safety across the board: at games, of course, but also at hotels, airports, and online. The new Collective Bargaining Agreement contains minimum safety requirements each team must have in place.There is a three-step process when a threat is reported. First, the league’s Global Security Operations Center, which operates on a 24/7 basis, assesses the validity of the threat and begins an investigation. The league next determines what additional security needs to be deployed to mitigate the threat. The third step includes potentially banning or restricting the threatening individual from arenas and games, or referring the case to local authorities. Every reported incident is investigated.“We’re going to care about what the prominent people in our society are doing,” Gabriel says. “And that’s good. There’s nothing bad about that. That’s like being an engaged person who cares about the world around them, and all the research that I’ve done and other people have done really suggests that this can be a really healthy part of life in the modern world.”The WNBA is working to ensure that when those relationships turn unhealthy, the problem is quickly dealt with.Explore more on these topicsWNBACaitlin ClarkBasketballUS sportsIndiana FeverfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Man City-bound 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan is MLS’s chaotic revelation  | MLS | The Guardian
description: The Philadelphia Union midfielder has gotten his longest run of game time since turning pro, and the data is tantalizing
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Philadelphia Union midfielder has gotten his longest run of game time since turning pro, and the data is tantalizing
Content: Cavan Sullivan’s talent has been a talking point for years.Photograph: Ron Smits/SOPA Images/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenCavan Sullivan’s talent has been a talking point for years.Photograph: Ron Smits/SOPA Images/ShutterstockMLSAnalysisMan City-bound 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan is MLS’s chaotic revelationJohn MullerThe Philadelphia Union midfielder has gotten his longest run of game time since turning pro, and the data is tantalizingTue 8 Sep 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 05.56 EDTShareThere’s avideofrom a United States U-15 camp three years ago that will make your head spin. It’s a routine training session for the boys on the pitch except one, a head shorter and a year or two younger than the others, who’s practicing with the national team for the first time.Is the boy nervous? He is not. A pass floats into the box and he checks his run, tries to get under it, but the ball is too high for his 13-year-old head to reach. He doesn’t even jump. As the cross sails over him, he flings himself forward like Superman and flicks a heel up behind his back, catching the ball with a scorpion kick that bounces straight into the path of a teammate for a cartoon assist.This is Cavan Sullivan: a player whose next move is difficult to predict, probably even for him. Which makes it even more remarkable that the predictions about him keep coming true.By now, you may have heard about him. Whispered about by scouts since childhood, signed before he had played a single minute as a pro to join Manchester City the day he turns 18, Sullivan became the youngest debutant in Major League Soccer history when he was 14. But raw potential doesn’t mean much at that age: the child star whose record he broke was none other than Freddy Adu, thegreat cautionary taleof American soccer.For two tantalizing years after he turned pro, Sullivan remained more a prophecy than a player, growing up on the Philadelphia Union’s bench. This summer, though, he got his shot, and in a recent run of starts he’s been rapidly, visibly maturing into the star who was promised. We finally have actual data on Sullivan and it’s very, very exciting.View image in fullscreenIllustration: John Muller / FutiJust getting on the pitch is already a promising sign. Of the 10 teenagers who have earned the most playing time inMLSsince 2015, eight have made the leap – with varying degrees of success – to Europe’s top five leagues. Sullivan isn’t there yet but he has by far the most minutes of any 16-year-old in that time and runs a close second to Adri Mehmeti, the 17-year-old currently bossing the New York Red Bulls’ midfield, at the next age up.Another leading indicator is how much his teammates trust him.“No matter what age you are, when a practice starts and guys give you the ball, that’s the ultimate sign of respect,” Sullivan’s first coach at the Union, Jim Curtin,said. “Within 10 seconds into the first training session, they gave him the ball.”That’s true in games, too. Sullivan takes 10.3% of his team’s touches, the most of any teenage MLS winger in at least a decade. Second place is Alphonso Davies, now of Bayern Munich, the best homegrown player the league has ever produced.Then of course there are the highlight numbers – four goals and three assists in MLS this season. Seven and seven in all competitions. Three and three in his last five games alone. Those are noisy stats, but the underlying numbers so far look just as bright: his 0.48 expected goals and assists per 90 minutes rank fourth among MLS teens with at least 1,000 minutes played, one spot below Jhon Duran, who broke the league transfer fee record when he moved to Aston Villa at 19.Advanced stats go deeper into Sullivan’s game. Player ratings infuti, a soccer stats app I co-created, use a model calledpossession valueto estimate how much every touch of the ball changes teams’ goal probabilities, so that a line-breaking pass in midfield, a goalline clearance or a dribble on the wing can all be added up in terms of their expected impact on the scoreline. The app adjusts these values based on how a player’s team plays with and without him, thenscales the ratingwithin his data-derived tactical role.According to futi ratings, Sullivan’s 2026 is the second-best of any MLS teenager on record, trailing only Gianluca Busio, now the captain of Venezia in Serie A, when he was three years older. The best 16-year-old MLS has ever seen isn’t just getting minutes and goals – he’s helping his team all over the pitch.When trying to describe a precocious, small, left-footed right-winger who loves to perform tricks, it’s too easy to reach for the most unfair comparison of all time, yet it’s a documented fact that Sullivanmodeledhis game after Lionel Messi (obligatory note: we’re not saying Sullivan has the same level of ability as the Argentinian). When Sullivan scored his first professional goal by slicing inside and curling a diagonal to an overlapping left-back before finishing a cutback from the penalty spot, it was impossible not to see Messi’s signature combination with Jordi Alba.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSullivan doesn’t play as centrally as Messi, though. Futi’s player style model classifies him as a “wide playmaker”; an attacker who likes to collect the ball out near the touchline and then break lines and create for teammates. He’s a ball-to-feet type who averages just 6.2 progressive receptions per 90 minutes and ranks in the 19th percentile among wide attackers for the directness of the passes he receives, meaning he’s not doing a lot of running in behind.What he’s doing instead, mostly, is dribbling. Sullivan’s style on the ball is less a young Messi and more like his other childhood hero, Alexis Sánchez: hips low, elbows out, juking defenders with feints, stutters, stepovers and changes of direction. He mixes in his weak foot to keep tacklers on their toes and applies a variety of touches to the ball, including a kid’s fair share of overly ambitious ones.The thing that makes his chaotic game hang together is an awareness of what’s going on around him. “I would say the big word is ‘playmaker,’” Sullivantold ESPNwhen he was 14. “That’s what I try and be every game, every training. I think I’m good on the dribble. My decision making is pretty good, and my vision on the field is one of my qualities.”Even when he’s squirming past defenders, Sullivan is preternaturally aware of his teammates’ runs and constantly looking to play them into dangerous spots. He averages 5.0 progressive passes per 90 minutes, top five among all MLS wide attackers. One of his trademark moves is dribbling across the defense and then snapping off a perfectly timed ball at an unexpected angle for a runner in the channel; another is trying some crazy lob over the back line, which occasionally comes off.The downside of this risky style of play is that he makes a lot of turnovers. The Union don’t really mind, though. Sullivan’s 65% pass completion rate is among the lowest in the league but about par for Philadelphia, the most direct team in MLS. It’s anyone’s guess how he might adapt to a totally different game at Man City.To even get there, he’ll have to answer some hard questions about his size and speed. Only 15 players in the Premier League last season were listed at or below Sullivan’s current 5ft 7in, and just one of them, Enzo Le Fée, was a starter in a similar role. Unlike Christian Pulisic, America’s last phenom to break through on the wing, Sullivan isn’t especially fast, which will be a tough sell in an increasingly physical European game.Then again, he’s been beating bigger, faster guys his whole life. Go back and watchthose old videosof this squib of a kid getting hip-checked by players twice his size, sprawling to the ground and somehow popping up with the ball velcroed to his feet. He is scrappy, relentless. As Bruce Arena once said of Clint Dempsey, Cavan Sullivan tries shit.Go ahead, just try to predict what he’ll do next.Explore more on these topicsMLSUSAManchester CityUS sportsPhiladelphia UnionanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Haaland double gives Manchester City ideal Champions League start in Porto | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Erling Haaland scored at the beginning and end of the second half to give Manchester City a 2-0 win in Porto, despite tempers flaring
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Erling Haaland scored at the beginning and end of the second half to give Manchester City a 2-0 win in Porto, despite tempers flaring
Content: Erling Haaland scores Manchester City’s second against Porto.Photograph: Luis Vieira/APView image in fullscreenErling Haaland scores Manchester City’s second against Porto.Photograph: Luis Vieira/APChampions LeagueHaaland double gives Manchester City ideal Champions League start in PortoJamie Jacksonat Estádio do DragãoTue 8 Sep 2026 17.08 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnzo Maresca admitted a liking for the “boom-boom” of house music in the buildup to this match, then enjoyed the sweet notes of victory having overseen a gritty performance from hisManchester Cityside in incessant rain.City had lost six of their past nine away games in the competition, and been beaten in the 2021Champions Leaguefinal at this venue, so to beat Porto and claim three points is a fillip for the manager’s nascent project.Mbappé and Valverde fire Real Madrid to Champions League win against InterRead moreA bust-up at half-time as the players and staff neared the tunnel may bring Uefa scrutiny, though. Images showed Rúben Dias placing a hand on what appeared to be Francesco Farioli, thePortohead coach. The defender did so as tempers frayed after a clash between Marc Guéhi and Gabriel Veiga that left the latter with a head injury, though he continued.Informed of Dias’s act, Maresca was visibly angered when asked if his captain will be spoken to, as it could cost City. “Probably, anyway you can ask what you want but how many times you see me or my bench or the guys that work with me stand up on the bench. Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times you see their bench?” he said.Overall, the Italian should feel exuberant. All four of his opening games have been won – maybe more than even the 46-year-old could have hoped for, Erling Haaland’s double maintaining the perfect start. The goalscoring phenomenon is now third on City’s all-time chart with 167 goals after only four years, with 59 in 59 Champions League matches.Haaland said: “Amazing game, against the champions of Portugal. We have to deliver on the biggest stage and we did that tonight.”Maresca gave Ayyoub Bouaddi a full debut, alongside Enzo Fernández in midfield, and the 18-year-old Moroccan impressed, though a failure to find Haaland brought a reprimand. “I told the chairman [Khaldoon al-Mubarak] we’ve got a gem there,” said Haaland. “But he should’ve played me through in the second half, I was all alone. I was a bit angry so I’ll tell him right now – but he played a good game, except that pass.”Initially, Porto could allow City to pitter-patter passes about as there was no quickness or penetration. Farioli’s men offered an example of how when Guéhi’s ball short-changed Bouaddi, possession was nabbed, and suddenly William Gomes had to be stopped on the edge of City’s area. Earlier, Veiga sliced through and had Gianluigi Donnarumma saving: the offside flag went up but here were two warnings.Quick GuideDortmund's Karetsas taken to hospitalShowBorussia Dortmund's Konstantinos Karetsas was taken to hospital after slumping to the turf 25 minutes into his Champions League debut against Villarreal.“Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems,” Dortmund said in a statement. “Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests.”The 18-year-old Greece international passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass. Karetsas was treated laying down then taken away on a stretcher. The score was 0-0 at the time.Dortmund went on to win 3-2 at home. Renato Veiga’s 53rd-minute own goal put the Bundesliga side ahead before Santiago Mouriño equalised in the 66th. Serhou Guirassy restored the lead in the 80th minute and scored the third with an 84th-minute penalty, before scoring an own goal in added time while trying to help in defence.Real Betistwice came from behind to beatLille3-2 away, ⁠with Marc Bartra scoring in the 34th and 49th minutes before Troy Parrott’s 54th-minute winner.Lille ​scored their opener in the 12th minute ‌and regained the lead through ‌Alexsandro in the 37th. The hosts later had Ethan Mbappé sent off for an elbow to ‌the face of an opponent.AEK Athens​made a winning start, beating the Austrian sideLASK1-0 in Greece thanks to Romanian midfielder Razvan Marin’s curling free-kick midway through the first half.AgenciesWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Discard the ponderous pace might have been Maresca’s message because when Phil Foden switched flanks from the right and accelerated, Porto were splayed, and Haaland’s header from the cross required Diogo Costa to keep the contest goalless.A near-carbon copy arrived when Antoine Semenyo popped the ball over from the left but, this time, Haaland’s header sailed over. City were warming up: Foden, Rayan Cherki and Haaland all being denied, as Porto were caught in a chokehold around their area.At Leicester and then Chelsea Maresca drew criticism for a quasi-sideways style. Yet tonight’s XI had become direct and a threat, as when Bouaddi chipped the ball left from near halfway, it went forward at speed, and a panicked Porto cleared.Now, when Veiga went down after the challenge with Guéhi, the match was halted and the discord that continued to the tunnel area started up.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionYet following the seemingly de rigueur fireworks before every Champions League game, Porto had begun with sky-high confidence after winning all of their five Primeira Liga outings, so when wandering off they remained content.The mood changed instantaneously on their return. City, at last, showed the ruthlessness needed at this level. Cherki, broke into the area, swerved left, leaving Costa stranded. He fed Fernández and Haaland headed the delivery into the turf and home and the visitors had a priceless lead.What would be Porto’s response? To rove upfield and go close to the equaliser, was the answer, a corollary of City’s openness, as when André Silva had an age to dip right and let fly, the former Portugal forward’s attempt hitting the side netting.View image in fullscreenErling Haaland outjumps Jakub Kiwior to head City into the lead.Photograph: Clive Brunskill/Getty ImagesThe lead was slender, as it was in Saturday’s 1-0 win over Coventry. Maresca acted when the hour passed, removing Cherki and Semenyo for Elliot Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye: two attackers for one forward and a holding player in Anderson whose role was to exert control and aid Bouaddi in snuffing out any Porto threat.A second goal would also stymie the hosts, so Ndiaye skipped across the grass and unloaded, but the effort went straight into Costa’s clutches. Foden, too, tried to break in behind, but the ball was shepherded back to the Porto keeper.Whenever Farioli’s team moved forward City remained vulnerable, despite Anderson’s presence. At the death, though, Haaland’s right-footed finish made sure of victory and meant that even when tempers flared again it was of zero import to Maresca’s team, who had emerged victorious on a difficult evening.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeaguePortoManchester CityEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: First-half treble powers Aston Villa to Champions League win at Club Brugge | Champions League | The Guardian
description: Goals from John McGinn, Emiliano Buendía and Nicholas Jackson secured Aston Villa a 3-2 victory against Club Brugge in their Champions League opener
Author: Ben Fisher
Headline: Goals from John McGinn, Emiliano Buendía and Nicholas Jackson secured Aston Villa a 3-2 victory against Club Brugge in their Champions League opener
Content: Nicolas Jackson takes the ball past Yann Sommer before scoring Aston Villa’s third goal.Photograph: Aston Villa/Aston Villa FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenNicolas Jackson takes the ball past Yann Sommer before scoring Aston Villa’s third goal.Photograph: Aston Villa/Aston Villa FC/Getty ImagesChampions LeagueFirst-half treble powers Aston Villa to Champions League win at Club BruggeBen Fisherat the Jan Breydel StadiumTue 8 Sep 2026 14.54 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAston Villa were 3-1 up after 43 minutes but were made to sweat for their first win of the season, emerging victorious from an entertaining Champions League opener with Club Brugge. John McGinn, who struck the only goal when Villa belatedly got their season up and runninglast September against Bologna, opened the scoring before Emi Buendía and a first goal for Nicolas Jackson in claret and blue appeared to put Villa out of sight at half-time.The Belgian side have become familiar foes since Villa returned to the big time, the glitziest club competition of them all; a freakish Tyrone Mings handball gifted the hosts a penalty, andsubsequently victory, in 2024-25 and on this occasion Aaron Wan-Bissaka conceded a second-half penalty to plunge a seesawing contest back into the balance.Mbappé and Valverde fire Real Madrid to Champions League win against InterRead more“Today was a very important step forward, being resilient when we were struggling,” said Unai Emery. “It is very important to start with three points. Hopefully it gives us confidence for the next matches, in the Premier League this Saturday against Nottingham Forest.”Emery had been at pains to radiate positivity despite another slow start – Villa picked up their first point of the Premier League season at the weekend and these goals represented their first of the campaign – but he was typically animated on the touchline in Brugge. He was particularly agitated midway through the second half when he felt, not for the first time this season, his substitutes were not ready for action. AtHull last weekend, it was Tammy Abraham and Wan-Bissaka, and a few days earlier Alejandro Garnacho against Arsenal.This time the culprits were Alysson, Ross Barkley and Lamare Bogarde. “In the dressing room at half-time we were speaking about some players who were tired, [Boubacar] Kamara, Wan-Bissaka,” Villa’s manager said. “I tried to keep [them on for] 15 minutes, but when I asked the players to replace [them] they were talking through the set pieces, sorting individual issues, but I needed quickly their impact on the field, and they did afterwards.”Quick GuideDortmund's Karetsas taken to hospitalShowBorussia Dortmund's Konstantinos Karetsas was taken to hospital after slumping to the turf 25 minutes into his Champions League debut against Villarreal.“Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems,” Dortmund said in a statement. “Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests.”The 18-year-old Greece international passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass. Karetsas was treated laying down then taken away on a stretcher. The score was 0-0 at the time.Dortmund went on to win 3-2 at home. Renato Veiga’s 53rd-minute own goal put the Bundesliga side ahead before Santiago Mouriño equalised in the 66th. Serhou Guirassy restored the lead in the 80th minute and scored the third with an 84th-minute penalty, before scoring an own goal in added time while trying to help in defence.Real Betistwice came from behind to beatLille3-2 away, ⁠with Marc Bartra scoring in the 34th and 49th minutes before Troy Parrott’s 54th-minute winner.Lille ​scored their opener in the 12th minute ‌and regained the lead through ‌Alexsandro in the 37th. The hosts later had Ethan Mbappé sent off for an elbow to ‌the face of an opponent.AEK Athens​made a winning start, beating the Austrian sideLASK1-0 in Greece thanks to Romanian midfielder Razvan Marin’s curling free-kick midway through the first half.AgenciesWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.In the end, it was a blend of old and new faces that got Villa over the line. Zion Suzuki made a couple of fine saves, João Gomes put in a typically tigerish performance and Jackson got the goal an encouraging all-round display deserved. The 19-year-old George Hemmings did not look out of place on hisChampions Leaguedebut. “The old players need to keep our standards high, to show everybody this is the only way we can achieve the process in our objectives and targets,” Emery said. “I am so happy.”Pau Torres was the unlikely catalyst for two of Villa’s three first-half goals. McGinn’s opener was a product of the centre-back roaming unchallenged to the edge of the box. Presumably it crossed Torres’s mind to shoot, though just as he was getting giddy, he spread play to McGinn, who guided a superb first-time, left-foot strike into the far corner of Yann Sommer’s goal. In starting on Tuesday night, the Swiss became just the second goalkeeper to represent five clubs in the Champions League, but it was a night to forget for the 37-year-old.View image in fullscreenJohn McGinn punches the air after giving Aston Villa an 11th-minute lead.Photograph: PA Wire/PAClub Brugge replied when the lively Jan Virgili found a way past Wan-Bissaka – who was making his full Villa debut – and located Hugo Vetlesen in the box, the Norway midfielder sending a crisp finish beyond Suzuki. The hosts were level for less than three minutes, a slick Villa move culminating in Buendía wheeling away in celebration. Jackson’s deft backheel supplied Gomes, who twisted inside the box and then picked out Buendía who did the rest.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionVilla’s third arrived a few minutes before the interval. Emery punched the air, his delight at establishing a two-goal advantage plain to see. Torres collected the ball on the edge of the Villa 18-yard box and, after shifting the ball out of his feet, he sent a lofted pass spinning into the opposition half, where Jackson got in between the opposition centre-backs, Lee Han-beom and Brandon Mechele. Enter Sommer, who raced about 40 yards from goal. Jackson swiped the ball cleanly and then was too strong for Lee before passing into an empty net.Things appeared rosy, but Villa had to withstand heavy pressure after a video assistant referee review led the Swiss referee, Sandro Schärer, to penalise Wan-Bissaka for handball in the box. Nicolò Tresoldi sent Suzuki the wrong way from the penalty spot and a few minutes later Suzuki pushed another shot on to the post.Victor Lindelöf tested the nerves of Emery, slicing a routine clearance when attempting to relieve the pressure. Villa, too, had chances, Jackson getting a shot away after latching on to a McGinn pass and Bogarde had a shot cleared off the line by the home full-back Joaquin Seys.Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueClub BruggeAston VillaEuropean club footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Newcastle progress as Joe Willock strikes late to see off Millwall | Carabao Cup | The Guardian
description: Joe Willock’s goal gave Newcastle a 1-0 win at Millwall that puts them into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: Joe Willock’s goal gave Newcastle a 1-0 win at Millwall that puts them into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup
Content: Joe Willock turns the ball into the net to win the game for Newcastle.Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJoe Willock turns the ball into the net to win the game for Newcastle.Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesCarabao CupNewcastle progress as Joe Willock strikes late to see off MillwallBarney Ronayat the DenTue 8 Sep 2026 17.07 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNewcastle did just enough in south-east London to progress to the next round of theCarabao Cup. Joe Willock scored the only goal of this boisterous, fun, slightly vague cup tie against a spirited Millwall team that was not so much down to the bare bones, as the bones beneath the bones.By the end there was a sense both sets of fans were more or less happy.Millwallfor the vigour of the performance and Newcastle for the result, the clean sheet and any signs of early progress in the dawning of the age of Jaissle-ball.Real Madrid cling on to beat Inter on Mourinho’s big Champions League nightRead more“We were worth it, we faced it, we did it,” was Matthias Jaissle’s verdict, having sent out a strong team, Jacob Ramsey coming in on the right for the early-season hot-hands Anthony Elanga. This was a significant win for Newcastle, who have been excitingly direct at times under their twinkly new manager, with his much-trailed blueprint for rapid transition, hyper-vertical attack and getting it forward quick-smart to the lads up front, but who still need to groove that system.Millwall also are not sure what they are yet this season, although this is more to do with injuries. They have 13 players out, which is at least an improvement on the previous 15. Absurdly, Alex Neil has already come under some pressure after a couple of losses. Football needs its irrational edge, but there is also a limit.Quick GuideCarabao Cup roundup: Rose gets his first winShowRyan Christie hit a hat-trick as Marco Rose celebrated his first win asBournemouthmanager with a 4-0 demolition ofLincolnin the Carabao Cup third round. Substitute Rayan completed the scoring against the Championship Imps at the Vitality Stadium.Jørgen Strand Larsen struck twice to propelCrystal Palaceto a 3-0 success overMiddlesbroughat Selhurst Park. Strand Larsen nodded home in each half before substitute Daichi Kamada lobbed Boro goalkeeper Sol Brynn to seal victory.Chemsdine Talbi scored the only goal to earnSunderlanda 1-0 win against Premier League rivalsHullat the Stadium of Light.Bradfordcame from behind to win 3-1 at fellow League One clubLeyton Orient. Goals from Will Swan, Stephen Humphrys and Nick Powell overturned a Macaulay Gillesphey own goal.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.At kick-off the sky was still a deep blackish blue above the lip of the Dockers Stand, the lights of the south London trains trundling past the unfilled corners of the ground. The Den was its usual self, a place that always manages somehow to generate that unique crackle of nonchalant hostility, no matter how midweek the crowd (and this one was a near-full house).View image in fullscreenIt was a pretty busy night down at The Den.Photograph: Ashley Western/Colorsport/ShutterstockNewcastle had most of the ball early on, but looked like what they are, a team still finding its shapes and rhythms. “They are PONY, Wall!” was one measured home fan assessment of the Jaissle project at this early stage.It is a fair point perhaps. Newcastle’s manager does have a very precise idea of the patterns and tempo-shifts he wants from his team. This sort of systems-football can lead to periods of drift while players learn the brief.Newcastle settled and began to dominate possession. Willock had the first real chance, snatching the ball from Romain Esse deep in the right-back zone and shooting powerfully but too close to Filip Marschall.In return Millwall offered graft, full-stretch defence and two deep banks of four in the classic old-school style. With 36 minutes gone Caleb Taylor headed just wide charging on to a nicely flighted free-kick, their first effort at goal. By half-time this had become something more like a cup tie as Millwall created pressure down the left, ratted and pressed nicely in midfield, and delivered some potent set pieces.Tino Livramento came on for Amar Dedic at the break. But it was Millwall who began at a clip, a zinging low cross from the right creating a scramble close to the Newcastle goalline, the ball eventually falling to Jenson Metcalfe, who shot with power just over the bar.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAfter which it was more diffuse pressure from Newcastle. Most teams would feel the absence of a midfielder of Bruno Guimarães’ passing quality. This one definitely does.View image in fullscreenMillwall’s Tairyk Arconte hits the post shortly before Newcastle’s goal.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersFor a while the game looked like it was, an early season cup distraction for two chop and change teams, no lack of energy, but all feints and ducks and grapples, like a boxer warming up in the mirror. By the hour mark Newcastle had 70% possession plus 17 shots at goal, but somehow Millwall’s collection of hurled together parts still looked more likely to create a telling chance.Elanga came on, a measure of Newcastle’s desire to get this done. Millwall had the best chance of the game up to that point on 79 minutes, Taïryk Arconte, a real menace on the right, hitting the post with a shot that pinged back on to Lukas Hornicek’s body but somehow stayed out.Moments later Newcastle scored with their first real moment of quality near goal. It was a lovely move to make it. Matias Fernandez-Pardo produced the key pass, a cute little shimmy and nudge outside to Lewis Hall. His cross found Willock in the centre, who finished it with a smart side-foot shot across the face of goal.Millwall continued to press, without finding much penetration and by the final whistle there was a concerted wave of noise coming from the full half-end of Newcastle fans, for whom the journey home into Wednesday morning would at least be a happy one.Explore more on these topicsCarabao CupMillwallNewcastle Unitedmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Championship roundup: West Ham go top after Bowen double sinks Bolton | Championship | The Guardian
description: Captain Jarrod Bowen scored twice as West Ham’s 3-2 win over Bolton took them top of the Championship on goal differenc
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Captain Jarrod Bowen scored twice as West Ham’s 3-2 win over Bolton took them top of the Championship on goal differenc
Content: Jarrod Bowen races away after hitting what proved to be the winning goal for West Ham at Bolton.Photograph: Paul Currie/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenJarrod Bowen races away after hitting what proved to be the winning goal for West Ham at Bolton.Photograph: Paul Currie/ShutterstockChampionshipChampionship roundup: West Ham go top after Bowen double sinks BoltonEngland forward scores twice in 3-2 victorySouthampton 3-1 Swansea; Watford 2-1 PrestonPress AssociationTue 8 Sep 2026 17.40 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 18.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleCaptain Jarrod Bowen scored twice asWestHam’s 3-2 win overBoltontook them top of theChampionshipon goal difference. The England international opened the scoring after 13 minutes and earned his side a first win at Bolton for 31 years with his second 13 minutes from time.In between, Wanderers, beaten for a fourth successive outing, equalised through midfielder Ethan Erhahon’s maiden goal for the club and they looked on course for a ninth successive league victory over the Hammers when Ruben Rodrigues converted a 27th-minute penalty. Instead, Konstantinos Mavropanos levelled with a 31st-minute header and Bowen completed the comeback.Real Madrid 2-1 Inter, Millwall 0-1 Newcastle: Champions League and Carabao Cup – as it happenedRead moreCyle Larin scored his fifth goal of the season asSouthamptonbeatSwansea3-1 to beat the side who were top of the table for the second home match in a row. Larin, who is the joint-top scorer in the Championship, found the net either side of Finn Azaz and Leo Scienza strikes to make it 13 games unbeaten at St Mary’s.Watfordshook off an awful first-half display to grab a 2-1 victory overPreston, who suffered their fifth defeat in six league games. Callum Lang had put the visitors ahead in the sixth minute as they threatened to overrun the Hornets, who hit back with two second-half goals in seven minutes from Edo Kayembe and Mamadou Doumbia.Wrexham’s wait for a home win goes on after they were held to a 1-1 draw by winlessBurnleywho sit one place off the bottom of the table. Jacques Ekomie headed in his second goal for the club since joining in a £7m deal from Angers, cancelling out Zeki Amdouni’s first-half effort for the Clarets who at least ended a run of seven straight away defeats dating back to last term.But it was a result that does little to help either side in their pursuit of promotion, withWrexhamhaving lost the momentum they carried into last season while Burnley face bigger problems after relegation from the top flight, having won only one league game since October. Former England striker Jamie Vardy joined this week, but the 39-year-old was suspended for this match as a result of yellow cards collected during his time with Italian side Cremonese.SheffieldUnitedreturned to winning ways after a display of ruthless finishing secured a 2-1 win atBlackburn. All the goals came in a first half that Rovers dominated and deservedly took the lead in through Kristi Montgomery’s first goal for the club on 20 minutes. The Blades turned the game on its head with goals from their only two shots of the half as Tom Cannon stroked home a second on this ground in two weeks in the 35th minute. Sydie Peck rifled home his first of the season a minute before the break to complete the turnaround.Cardiff’s winless start to the season continued asStokeheld on for a 1-1 draw in the Welsh capital and their first away point since January. Stoke had hope of an away-day success after a run of nine straight Championship defeats when Ben Johnson scored midway through the first half. But the Potters came under fierce pressure in the second half and Joel Colwill’s headed home for Cardiff hosts who hit a post three times. The draw – Cardiff’s fourth in six games – was enough to take the home side out of the relegation zone, while Stoke slip to 15th.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipBlackburn RoversSheffield UnitedCardiff CityStoke CitySouthamptonSwansea CitynewsShareReuse this content

title: Air traffic chaos delays Arsenal flight to Naples for Champions League | Champions League | The Guardian
description: The team arrived late at their hotel in Italy and did not hold a press conference for a game where Jurriën Timber is in the squad for the first time since May
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: The team arrived late at their hotel in Italy and did not hold a press conference for a game where Jurriën Timber is in the squad for the first time since May
Content: Mikel Arteta talks to his players in training before their delayed flight to Italy.Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMikel Arteta talks to his players in training before their delayed flight to Italy.Photograph: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesChampions LeagueAir traffic chaos delays Arsenal flight to Naples for Champions LeagueTeam arriving late at their hotel in southern ItalyJurriën Timber in squad for first time since MayEd Aaronsin NaplesTue 8 Sep 2026 14.38 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleArsenal’s preparations for their opening Champions League game against Napoli have been disrupted after they were caught up in thetravel chaos that affected airportsacross the UK.Mikel Arteta was forced to cancel his pre-match press conference at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Tuesday after Arsenal’s flight was severely delayed by an air-traffic control issue. The Arsenal manager and his players are understood to have remained at the club’s training ground in Hertfordshire as they waited for the delay to pass after completing their morning session as usual.‘Relief’ of Premier League title has given Arsenal confidence, says David RayaRead moreClub sources have insisted there has been no alteration to their planned schedule other than arriving later than expected to the team hotel. Uefa has also agreed to allowArsenalto cancel their mandatory press conference due to the delays, which have also affected supporters travelling to Italy for the match.Jurriën Timber is set to be part of the Arsenal squad for the first time since theChampions Leaguefinal defeat by Paris Saint-Germain on 30 May after recovering from a groin injury. The Netherlands defender missed the World Cup due to the problem that has dogged him since March but Arteta said before Sunday’s win over Chelsea that Timber was close to returning.Cristhian Mosquera is still absent with a muscle issue but Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who signed his first professional deal last month, is also part of the 23-man squad.Arsenal won all eight of their group stage matches in the Champions League last season on their way to the final and have only lost one in their last 12 away games in the competition. But as they prepare for one of Europe’s most intimidating atmospheres, Arteta insisted they must take one game at a time despite starting the season with a 100% record in the Premier League.“That puts us in a really good situation. The energy and the confidence around the team is high – now we have to show that,” he said.“I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create. The record at home is really, really strong. We know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionNapoli finished as runners up behind Inter in Serie A last season, but have made a poor start this season under their new manager, Massimiliano Allegri. Kevin De Bruyne is expected to feature against Arsenal but they are without Scott McTominay, who had a successful surgical procedure to treat an irregular heartbeat yesterday. The 29-year-old is expected to resume training in two weeks.Napoli are also are likely to be without influential former Fulham midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa as Allegri takes charge of his first Champions League match for four years. “People in this town have passion for the team, we have to start winning games again,” Allegri said. “We know we are challenging a very strong team – Arteta has done extraordinary things. Let’s face it with pride and desire.”Explore more on these topicsChampions LeagueArsenalMikel ArtetaNapolinewsShareReuse this content

title: Harry Kane and Alessia Russo among nominees for this year’s Ballon d’Or  | Ballon d'Or | The Guardian
description: Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice have been nominated for this year’s men’s Ballon d’Or while Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood have been nominated for the women’s award
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice have been nominated for this year’s men’s Ballon d’Or while Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood have been nominated for the women’s award
Content: Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane and Alessia Russo of Arsenal.Composite: FC Bayern/Getty Images; WSL/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenBayern Munich’s Harry Kane and Alessia Russo of Arsenal.Composite: FC Bayern/Getty Images; WSL/Getty ImagesBallon d'OrHarry Kane and Alessia Russo among nominees for this year’s Ballon d’OrBellingham, Rice and Alex Greenwood also nominatedCeremony to move from Paris to London for 2026 awardsGuardian sportTue 8 Sep 2026 12.11 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHarry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice have been nominated for this year’s men’s Ballon d’Or with Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood nominated for the women’s award.The 30 men’s and 30 women’s nominees were revealed by France Football magazine on Tuesday, with the winners to be announced at a ceremony in London on 26 October. Ousmane Dembélé, who won the men’s award last year, has been nominated again, as has hisFrance teammate Kylian Mbappé, who made history when he overtook Lionel Messi for all-time World Cup goals (22) at this summer’s tournament.Who should win the men’s Ballon d’Or?Read moreIn the women’s field, two-time winner Alexia Putellas, Ewa Pajor and Melchie Dumornay are among the favourites to succeed Aitana Bonmatí. Winner of the past three awards, Bonmatí did not make the cut after missing most of the season through injury. The Spaniard returned at the end of Barcelona’s quadruple-winning season that included another Champions League title.Kane is odds-on to win the men’s award after a club-record 61 goals in 51 games for German double winners Bayern Munich last season. He also scored six times at the World Cup for England, a tournament where Bellingham and Rice shone as well, the latter also playing a key role in Arsenal ending a 22-year wait for the Premier League title.Quick GuideBallon d'Or nominees: the full listShowMen's awardJude Bellingham, Pau Cubarsí, Marc Cucurella, Ousmane Dembélé, Luis Díaz, Bruno Fernandes, Gabriel, Erling Haaland, Achraf Hakimi, Harry Kane, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Lamine Yamal, Sadio Mané, Marquinhos, Lautaro Martínez, Kylian Mbappé, Nuno Mendes, Lionel Messi, João Neves, Michael Olise, Willian Pacho, Julián Quiñones, Declan Rice, Rodri, Fabián Ruiz, William Saliba, Ferran Torres, Dayot Upamecano, Vinícius Jr., Vitinha.Women's awardSelma Bacha, Barbra Banda, Klara Buhl, Esmee Brugts, Mariona Caldentey, Scarlett Camberos, Kerstin Casparij, Temwa Chawinga, Cata Coll, Melchie Dumornay, Caroline Graham Hansen, Alex Greenwood, Patri Guijarro, Pernille Harder, Yui Hasegawa, Rose Lavelle, Mapi León, Lorena, Melvine Malard, Manaka Matsukubo, Vivianne Miedema, Ewa Pajor, Claudia Pina, Alexia Putellas, Wendie Renard, Alessia Russo, Khadija Shaw, Momoko Tanikawa, Caroline Weir, Tessa Wullaert.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Lamine Yamal, who won La Liga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain, is second favourite to win the award, followed by his club and international teammate Rodri. Messi, who has a record eight Ballon d’Or awards, is on the shortlist after guiding Argentina to the World Cup final and winning Major League Soccer with Inter Miami.Russo finished third in last year’s voting and enjoyed another successful individual campaign, scoring 24 goals in 40 club appearances. Greenwood, the Manchester City captain, lifted the Women’s Super League and FA Cup last season.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThe Ballon d’Or ceremony is moving from its traditional Paris home to London this year to mark the 70th anniversary of the first award won by England great Stanley Matthews.Explore more on these topicsBallon d'OrHarry KanenewsShareReuse this content

title: More than 100,000 people add names to complaint against Gianni Infantino | Fifa | The Guardian
description: The letter alleges the Fifa president ‘has, at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty in his efforts to ingratiate himself’ with Donald Trump
Author: Paul MacInnes
Headline: The letter alleges the Fifa president ‘has, at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty in his efforts to ingratiate himself’ with Donald Trump
Content: Gianni Infantino will seek re-election as Fifa president next year.Photograph: Kacper Pempel/ReutersView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino will seek re-election as Fifa president next year.Photograph: Kacper Pempel/ReutersFifaMore than 100,000 people add names to complaint against Gianni InfantinoLetter alleges Fifa president ‘has abused his power’Donald Trump links and FFE scandal among objectionsPaul MacInnesTue 8 Sep 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMore than 100,000 people have added their names to a complaint againstGianni Infantino, alleging the Fifa president has “at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty” through his interactions with Donald Trump.TheReboot Fifa campaignwas launched before the World Cup with the aim of delivering “the biggest complaint Fifa has ever received” over the organisation’s alleged failings of governance. The campaign has since extended the scope of its accusations to includethe reversal of the ban for Folarin Balogunat the tournament andthe aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.Embattled Fifa president Infantino declares intention to stand for re-electionRead moreThe complaint was submitted on Tuesday to Fifa’s ethics committee and in a supporting letter the organisers of RebootFifa, the advocacy group Fair Square, call on the committee to take action. An original complaint, submitted in December of last year, failed to receive a response from the committee but has gained the backing of the Norwegian football federation and 50 European parliamentarians.“The fact that 100,000 individuals added their names to this call for accountability is clear evidence of mounting public concern,” the Fair Square letter said. “As the independent judicial body tasked with the critical task of upholding the ‘integrity and reputation of football’, the ethics committee must not only act, it must be seen to act with appropriate haste, transparency and rigour.”The letter lists eight incidents that form the basis of the Reboot Fifa complaint, which Fair Square alleges “provide compelling evidence that the Fifa president has, at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty in his efforts to ingratiate himself with the US president.”. The incidents include the Balogun affair – where Trump admitted he asked Fifa to review the US striker’s red card – and the FFE scandal. They also citethe awarding of the Fifa peace prize to Trump, Infantino’s involvement in Trump’s Board of Peace in the Middle East and the Fifa president’s promise to work with Trump to “make not only America great again but also the entire world”, an act Fair Square suggests shows a failure to remain politically neutral.Fifa, when approached for comment, pointed to a statement first published a month ago. “It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president,” the statement said.“Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFifa confirmed on Sunday that Infantino would be seeking re-election for a fourth and final term next year despite pressure from Uefa and criticism from within the Asian confederation and Concacaf (the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation). Uefa has called on Infantino to stand down and recently announcedits intention to pursue criminal claimsin the US over the FFE plans.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoDonald TrumpFootball politicsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Alexis Mac Allister ‘very sad’ Liverpool have not offered him a new contract | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Alexis Mac Allister has said he feels “very sad” after Liverpool declined to offer him a new contract and admitted he rejected the chance to leave this summer
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Alexis Mac Allister has said he feels “very sad” after Liverpool declined to offer him a new contract and admitted he rejected the chance to leave this summer
Content: Alexis Mac Allister joined Liverpool from Brighton in June 2023 and has two years remaining on his contract with the club.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAView image in fullscreenAlexis Mac Allister joined Liverpool from Brighton in June 2023 and has two years remaining on his contract with the club.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PALiverpoolAlexis Mac Allister ‘very sad’ Liverpool have not offered him a new contractMidfielder rejected chance to leave the club in summer‘ I will give 100% until my last day’ says 27-year-oldAndy HunterTue 8 Sep 2026 10.04 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAlexis Mac Allister has said he feels “very sad” afterLiverpooldeclined to offer him a new contract and admitted he rejected the chance to leave this summer.Mac Allister revealed unhappiness over his contract situation before Liverpool’s Champions League opener against Atlético Madrid on Wednesday. The Argentina midfielder has two years remaining on his deal and believes he is effectively playing for a new contract having been informed no extension is on the table. Mac Allister confirmed he had offers to leave – Real Madrid and Manchester City were among those linked – but chose to stay because Liverpool can accomplish “something special” this season under Andoni Iraola.“There was a chance [to leave] of course, like everybody knows,” said the 27-year-old, clearly keen to get the matter off his chest. “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very sad. I think everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club, every single day in training. Of course I have good games and bad games, but I always give my best.Liverpool agree £60m-a-year shirt sponsorship deal with Turkish AirlinesRead more“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts, which makes me very happy because they deserve it, but at the same time it makes me sad that I didn’t get mine. Of course there is still time [to be offered a new contract]. Fans don’t need to worry because I will give 100% until my last day. We will see what happens. There was options to leave this summer. I think right now I’m in the right club.”Liverpool signed Mac Allister for acut-price £35m in June 2023by activating a release clause in his Brighton contract, which meant he was on a lucrative salary from the moment he arrived at Anfield. He claimed a new deal from Liverpool “is going to depend on how I perform during these years,” although he will be approaching 30 by the time his existing contract expires.Asked why he chose to stay at Anfield this summer, despite his obvious discontent, Mac Allister said: “Because this is the right club, that’s why. I love being here, this is something special. I feel we can be successful, what I want is to win trophies and I think we have the right players and the right mentality to do great things, but everyone had to be on the same page.”Mac Allister’s negotiating position would not have been at its strongest this summer after a disappointing season under Arne Slot, although he enjoyed a fine World Cup with Argentina. Iraola suggested Liverpool’s decision on Mac Allister may not be final.The head coach, who will take charge of his first Champions League game on Wednesday while Diego Simeone leads Atlético for the 129th time in the competition, said: “I don’t know how much my players earn. I know how to improve my players, to help them win games. The same with Alexis and everyone else. He is very experienced player who has achieved massive things, but I hope he can develop as a player and if all goes well those problems will be solved.”Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolnewsShareReuse this content

title: Sabalenka shows fighting spirit to deny Noskova and reach US Open semis | US Open Tennis 2026 | The Guardian
description: Defending US Open champion Aryna Sabalenka said she pushed herself to the limit in fighting back from 4-2 down in the final set to beat Linda Noskova and reach the semi-finals
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: Defending US Open champion Aryna Sabalenka said she pushed herself to the limit in fighting back from 4-2 down in the final set to beat Linda Noskova and reach the semi-finals
Content: Aryna Sabalenka lets it all out after battling past Linda Noskova in the quarter-finals of the US Open.Photograph: Sarah Yenesel/EPAView image in fullscreenAryna Sabalenka lets it all out after battling past Linda Noskova in the quarter-finals of the US Open.Photograph: Sarah Yenesel/EPAUS Open Tennis 2026Sabalenka shows fighting spirit to deny Noskova and reach US Open semisDefending champion wins 7-6 (1), 3-6, 7-6 (7)Sabalenka: ‘I was pushing myself to the limit’Tumaini Carayolat Flushing MeadowsTue 8 Sep 2026 16.17 EDTLast modified on Tue 8 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt seemed for some time that Aryna Sabalenka would be consumed by the rage and anxiety that has smothered her for so much of the year. At 2-2 in the final set of her brutal quarter-final against Linda Noskova, a second double fault of the game damned Sabalenka to a 0-40 deficit. She instantly fell to her knees, bowed her head and screamed. She soon trailed 2-4 in the set.Over her past five arduous months, Sabalenka has reliably unravelled under pressure. However, at the final grand slam tournament of the year, with her US Open title and No 1 ranking on the line, this was her very last chance to salvage her season. Somehow, the top-seeded Sabalenka finally had a response as she recovered to win an astonishing match and reach the semi-finals with a 7-6 (1), 3-6, 7-6 (7) win over Noskova, the sixth seed.US Open 2026 quarter-finals: Tiafoe v Michelsen after Sabalenka edges out Noskova – liveRead moreBefore the tournament, it was clear that the intense depth at the top of the women’s game, where each of the top 11 players currently hold a big title, meant there are so many worthy title candidates. The quarter-final lineup reflects this embarrassment of riches. Each of the top six seeds reached the last eight, with five of them being grand slam champions along with the perennial top-five player Jessica Pegula and the Olympic gold medallist Zheng Qinwen.A meeting between the defending US Open champion and the new Wimbledon champion was top of the list of the highly anticipated tussles and it developed into one of the best matches of the year. This was a spectacular exhibition of unfiltered first-strike tennis. The quality of serving from both sides of the net was supreme, with Noskova firing down 18 aces and Sabalenka finishing with 46% unreturned serves, including a statement second-serve ace to close out a tight tie-break set. Both players fearlessly forced themselves inside the baseline, Sabalenka’s searing power contrasted with Noskova’s sweet timing and precise changes of direction.After trailing 2-4, 0-15, Sabalenka followed up a commanding service game with a flawless return game, pulling herself level with a break to love. Even under intense pressure, Sabalenka continued to think clearly as she kept testing the hitchy Noskova forehand which, despite being strong for much of the match, buckled in the decisive moments deep in the final set and marked the difference between them. “What a battle,” said Sabalenka. “What an incredible player she is. I’m speechless right now because I was pushing myself to the limit in this match, especially in the third set. I honestly thought that that’s it, the match is over. Probably that’s what helped me to feel loose and go after my shots. Super happy to get this win.”Sabalenka’s victory leaves the pressure on Elena Rybakina’s shoulders as she tries to usurp Sabalenka in the rankings. Should Rybakina defeat Zheng in their quarter-final on Wednesday, the Kazakhstani will become world No 1 for the first time. If she loses, Sabalenka, Coco Gauff or Jessica Pegula would finish the tournament ranked No 1 if they win the title. While the ranking is out of her hands, Sabalenka’s resilience means she is still in the running for a third consecutive US Open title. She will face the winner of the all-American night battle between the third seed Pegula and Emma Navarro, the 26th seed.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAlthough Noskova did not depart Arthur Ashe Stadium with a victory, after struggling with motivation after her life-changing Wimbledon triumph, reaching the quarter-finals of her next grand slam tournament and performing at such a high level against the world No 1 is a statement of intent. As she adjusts to her new status at the top of the game, the 21-year-old will only continue to improve and to make life hell for the established elite.Explore more on these topicsUS Open Tennis 2026TennisUS Open tennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: County cricket: title race hots up while Leicestershire charged by ECB – as it happened | County Championship | The Guardian

Content: 6h ago15.13 EDTTanya's roundupThe three leading contenders for the Division One title, Somerset, Warwickshire andNottinghamshire, each had a profitable day, thoughWarwickshireswung the biggest hammer after dismissingGlamorganfor 69 at Sophia Gardens.Ethan Bamber was chief destroyer, with five for 28, passing 50 wickets for the season, while Ed Barnard (three for five) provided able backup.
